# Vendored JPEG decoder

This directory contains the library source and manifests from the `jpeg-decoder` 0.3.2 crates.io release, upstream image-rs/jpeg-decoder commit `eb2d7c0f6a2d0298aba7a7f8b9ca1440353e8f8c`. The downloaded crate SHA-256 is `00810f1d8b74be64b13dbf3db89ac67740615d6c891f0e7b6179326533011a07`. Upstream is dual licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0; both original license files are retained. Upstream examples, benches and external tests/assets are omitted. The library source, README, Cargo manifests and VCS identity otherwise match the release except for the exact patch in [UPSTREAM-PATCH.diff](UPSTREAM-PATCH.diff). The adapter disables default features, including Rayon. Upstream declares Rust 1.61; the adapter's pinned image 0.25.10 requires Rust 1.88, which also supports the manifest's check-cfg declaration.

The upstream decoder pads Huffman lookahead with zero bits after a marker and permits those synthetic bits to be consumed as entropy. This accepted a JPEG whose 549 entropy bytes were truncated to five while retaining EOI. zune-jpeg 0.5.15 with strict mode also accepted the same fixture. The patch tracks real entropy bits separately, rejects consuming synthetic bits through the four existing Result-returning consumption paths, and resets accounting at restart markers. Harmless lookahead padding remains available. One pre-existing trailing space in an upstream documentation comment is removed so repository whitespace checks remain clean. The only manifest change declares the legacy upstream `target_arch="asmjs"` cfg value to modern rustc without disabling the check-cfg lint.

The adapter validates bounded encoded bytes, dimensions, pixel count and a conservative decoded allocation budget before full decode. It requires consumption of exactly one JPEG through its EOI marker. The adapter's tests retain generated baseline, progressive, restart and byte-stuffed JPEG fixtures, missing-EOI and truncated-entropy negatives, and every truncated baseline entropy prefix. The patch is independent of any native screenshot helper and does not establish graphical acceptance.

`UPSTREAM-FILES.json` records the registry and vendored SHA-256 for every retained upstream file. The patch uses zero context and a Git binary delta for the whitespace-only documentation change, preserving exact upstream bytes without introducing trailing whitespace into the patch artifact. Apply or reverse it with `git apply --binary --unidiff-zero` (add `-R` to reverse); the reverse operation and every file hash were checked against the downloaded crate source.
